items.title: Nick Brignola interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, July 28, 1997
items.q: Joe Farrell and I used to play club dates and then it’d be like twelve, one o’clock in the morning and we’d get on the subway and go up to Harlem and sit in up there.

ctx.x: Joe Farrell and I used to play club dates and then it’d be like twelve, one o’clock in the morning and we’d get on the subway and go up to Harlem and sit in up there. And we were accepted, you know, I mean we weren’t — if we were jazz musicians you were in. Nobody bothered us and I mean you felt completely safe, within reason, I mean there’s always some —
Well I’m glad you brought that up because I’ve been curious about the racial interaction in jazz and if it’s changed over the years.
